observation: One undivided monochrome schematic. Three vertically separated, near-horizontal solid strokes labelled a, b, c at their left ends. The upper a and middle b have similar solid extents ending at the right near the same x-coordinate. At those ends a continues as a descending dashed stroke and b as an ascending dashed stroke; those dashed portions cross at the labelled P and continue beyond it. c is a lower solid stroke extending farther right than the solid a/b portions, with no dashed continuation. The dashed portions visibly change direction relative to the solid portions. No grid, arrowheads, numerical data, parallel marks or angle marks.
interpretationBoundary: The solid-to-dashed direction changes are source facts of the schematic. They cannot by themselves be declared collinear extensions of straight Euclidean lines. The status of P and the supposed line intersection is UNKNOWN until the full proof is read.
unknown: Whether P is a supposed and refuted intersection rather than an actual one.
Whether the proof states a parallel c and b parallel c.
Whether dashed portions are symbolic hypothetical continuations.
No separate mathematical point marker at P is reliably distinguishable from the dashed-stroke crossing.
